hero.lede: I'm Luis Talavera — a developer building thoughtful, performant interfaces from Lima, Perú.

work.lede: A short trail of products, tools and pages I've designed or shipped in the last few years.

skills.lede: Frontend by default, with enough backend, tooling and process to ship end-to-end.

about.lede: I care about how an interface feels under the finger — the rhythm of an animation, the weight of a typeface, the quiet of an empty state.
about.p1: I've spent the last few years building e-commerce experiences in VTEX and shipping React apps end-to-end. Before that, I co-built the developer-evaluation platform at Codeable, where I learned to balance speed with the kind of polish a learner actually trusts.
about.p2: Outside of work I'm usually in the browser dev tools, the terminal, or — more recently — a sketchbook trying to design before I code.

footloose.name: Footloose
footloose.description: Current work — frontend on the Footloose e-commerce store. I lead redesigns, mobile adaptations and new landings on VTEX. Where VTEX components fall short, I drop into custom React to keep the brand and the conversion intact.

codeable.name: Codeable evaluation
codeable.description: Owned the React frontend of the registration + evaluation flow for Codeable applicants. Scored coding and English: timed attempts, an embedded code editor, retry logic. The Ruby on Rails API handled the heavy validation.

personal.name: This site
personal.description: An ongoing playground I rebuild whenever I learn something new. Currently React + Vite + Framer Motion + Lenis. Source is on GitHub — feedback always welcome.

frontend.name: Frontend
frontend.description: React for interactive surfaces, TypeScript for guard rails, SCSS or Tailwind for systems. I lean on Framer Motion for motion and care a lot about the small details — focus rings, scroll behavior, prefers-reduced-motion.

backend.name: Backend
backend.description: Started on Ruby + Rails — full-stack apps and APIs through my Codeable years. Relational (PostgreSQL) and document (Firebase) stores. Comfortable owning a small API end-to-end.

github.name: GitHub & CI
github.description: Long-time Git user, including GitHub Actions for CI, GitHub Pages for static deploys (this site, included). Clean histories, reviewable PRs, conventional commits where it fits.

agile.name: Agile
agile.description: Trained in Scrum and shipped against it in teams. Funny enough, I'd been running sprint-shaped weeks with classmates before I knew the name for it. Process should serve the team — not the other way around.
